h1: What legal hardship standard is required to get a zoning variance in Newton, MA?
title: Massachusetts and Newton Zoning Variances: The Legal Hardship Test
description: Review the three statutory findings a zoning authority must make before granting a variance.
short_answer: Massachusetts General Laws Chapter 40A, Section 10 sets a strict variance test. The authority must find special circumstances involving the soil conditions, shape, or topography of the land or structure; substantial hardship from literal enforcement; and that relief can be granted without substantial detriment to the public good or substantial derogation from zoning's purpose. A variance is not simply permission to avoid an inconvenient rule.

facts.text: The statute requires circumstances relating to soil conditions, shape, or topography that particularly affect the land or structure and do not generally affect the zoning district.

The authority must find substantial hardship from literal enforcement and determine that relief can be granted without substantial detriment to the public good or substantial derogation from the ordinance's purpose.

qa.q: Is financial cost alone enough to prove a zoning variance hardship?
qa.a: The statute requires the specified land or structure circumstances as well as substantial hardship and the public-good findings. Financial cost alone is not the complete statutory test.
